issue.title: [Medium][Migration] Unpublish unintended legacy Pages deployment without deleting preserved history
issue.body:
<!-- nativeCmpkit-operational:pages-unpublish-20261024 -->
## Classification

**Medium priority — confirmed migration/hosting control incident, not an additional baseline library defect.** Existing deployment unpublishing requires the repository owner's GitHub UI action. Legacy branch publishing has already been disabled. No releases or packages were published.

## Evidence and affected configuration

- Destination: `Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit`; Pages initially reported `build_type=legacy`, source `gh-pages:/`.
- GitHub deployment **7300258890**, actor `github-pages[bot]`, recorded success at **2026-10-24T14:58:51Z**.
- Source is the preserved historical commit **2c3055c523ed6efe183d828b7a7942d357cd4d29**, not the new nativeCmpkit documentation.
- Three `DELETE /repos/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/pages` requests returned definitive HTTP422: `Deactivating GitHub pages for this repository is not allowed.` This persisted after changing publishing mode to `workflow` and trying the current documented API version.
- [Incident narrative](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.md), [structured incident](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.json), and linked API/status receipts retain exact IDs, timestamps, responses and ref verification.

## Root cause and impact

The historical publishing branch was selected by legacy Pages hosting; disabling GitHub Actions alone did not establish that Pages was inactive. The exact internal activation mechanism is not proven. GitHub recorded a successful bot deployment during ref import although no migration command requested a deployment.

An old upstream site may be available under the owner's project route, contrary to the migration's no-deployment intent. Public reachability/content and CDN cache expiration were not verified. No secret disclosure or exploit is established.

## Recommended action

1. Open [Settings → Pages](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/settings/pages) and select **Unpublish site** next to the current deployment.
2. **Do not delete, rename or force-push `gh-pages`**: preserving its original ref and history is a migration requirement.
3. Keep `build_type=workflow`; current verification workflows have read-only permissions and no Pages deployment step. Leave Actions disabled outside supervised verification.
4. Append an observed resolution to the incident record, retaining the failed API attempts and original deployment history.

GitHub documents [unpublishing as separate from deleting configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/unpublishing-a-github-pages-site). The owner has already been asked; no response or completed action is assumed.

## Verification / risks

- Verify the existing deployment is unpublished; distinguish owner confirmation, API state and any independent URL check. Do not infer that `has_pages=true/false` alone proves CDN content expiration.
- Recheck the original `gh-pages` SHA and every preserved non-main branch/tag.
- Confirm no additional deployments or publishing workflows were triggered.
- Preserve all incident receipts; do not rewrite history to conceal the event.

Effort: **S**, administrative; dependency: owner UI access because the public REST deletion route refused the request. This operational follow-up is separate from the 164 baseline findings and 170 managed audit/history issues, avoiding a duplicate or misleading reopening of BUILD-008.
